body.translated_text: // Homage to the Great Compassionate One //

children.translated_text: The <s>dharma</s>-teaching of the <s>Buddhas</s> relies upon two truths:

children.text: lokasaṃvṛtisatyaṃ ca satyaṃ ca paramārthataḥ // Sda_1 //
children.translated_text: the conventional truth of the world (<s>lokasaṃvṛtisatya</s>) and the truth in the ultimate sense (<s>paramārthasatya</s>). // Sda_1 //

children.text: saṃvṛttirmanyate dvedhā mithyā ca tathatā tathā /
children.translated_text: The conventional (<s>saṃvṛti</s>) is considered twofold: the false and the real (<s>tathatā</s>);
the first is again twofold: [appearances such as] the reflected moon, and wrong reasoning from faulty doctrines. // Sda_2 //
That which is delightful without analysis, possessing the nature of destruction and arising,
and capable of effective action (<s>arthakriyāsamartha</s>)—that is regarded as real conventional truth (<s>tathatā-saṃvṛti</s>). // Sda_3 //

children.text: eka evaparo hyarthaḥ paraiśca dvividho mataḥ /
children.translated_text: There is indeed only one supreme reality, though others consider it twofold;

children.text: na kācid dharmatā siddhā kuto dvitryādikaṃ bhavet // Sda_4 //
children.translated_text: not a single <s>dharmatā</s> (nature of things) is established—how then could a second, third, or more exist? // Sda_4 //
Non-arising, cessation, and so forth are characterized by the words of [the Buddha's] teaching;

children.text: paramārthābhinnaśīlatvān naiva dharmā na dharmatā // Sda_5 //
children.translated_text: since [they are] of a nature inseparable from ultimate reality (<s>paramārtha</s>), [there are] neither <s>dharmas</s> nor <s>dharmatā</s>. // Sda_5 //
In <s>śūnyatā</s> (emptiness), not even the slightest distinction exists;
since awakening (<s>bodhi</s>) is free from conceptual elaboration (<s>nirvikalpa</s>), it is called the view of <s>śūnyatā</s>. // Sda_6 //
It is stated in the profound <s>sūtra</s>: that seeing is [in fact] non-seeing;

children.text: tatra draṣṭā na dṛśyaṃ cāpyanādinidhanaṃ śivam // Sda_7 //
children.translated_text: therein there is neither seer nor seen—[it is] without beginning or end, auspicious (<s>śiva</s>). // Sda_7 //
Free from conceptual elaboration (<s>nirvikalpa</s>), without support (<s>nirālamba</s>), devoid of existence and non-existence,
without foundation, without basis, incomparable, beyond coming and going. // Sda_8 //
Inexpressible, without appearance, unchanging, unconditioned (<s>asaṃskṛta</s>),
accessible [only] to yogins—this [reality] is free from the obscurations of afflictions (<s>kleśāvaraṇa</s>) and of the knowable (<s>jñeyāvaraṇa</s>). // Sda_9 //
Direct perception (<s>pratyakṣa</s>) and inference (<s>anumāna</s>)—that pair is accepted in the Buddhist [tradition];
that <s>śūnyatā</s> is accessible through both [of these] is the speech of delusion by those of limited vision. // Sda_10 //
Knowledge of <s>dharmatā</s> would then follow even for non-Buddhist (<s>tīrthika</s>) and <s>śrāvaka</s> [practitioners];
what then need be said of the <s>Vijñānavādins</s>?—there would be no contradiction for the <s>Mādhyamika</s>. // Sda_11 //
Then all doctrines would be equal in having valid means of knowledge and objects of knowledge;
since <s>dharmatā</s>, even as an object of valid cognition, contradicts all logical reasoning. // Sda_12 //

children.text: bāhulyena kathaṃ na syāt pratyakṣaṃ cānumā vṛthā /
children.translated_text: How could it not generally [be the case that] direct perception [is insufficient], and inference would be futile?
For the purpose of refuting the claims of non-Buddhists, the learned have composed [their] treatises. // Sda_13 //
It is not apprehended through either conceptual or non-conceptual cognition;

children.text: āgame 'pi sphuṭaṃ vidvānācāryo bhavya āha ca // Sda_14 //
children.translated_text: the learned master <s>Ācārya</s> [Dharmakīrti], an authority (<s>bhavya</s>), has clearly stated this in [his] <s>Āgama</s> as well. // Sda_14 //
By whom was <s>śūnyatā</s> understood? It was explicated by the <s>Tathāgatas</s>;
indeed <s>Nāgārjuna</s>, the disciple of the Serpent [beings], is the seer of the truth of <s>dharmatā</s>. // Sda_15 //
Thereafter, through successive traditions, the truth of <s>dharmatā</s> is accessible;
eighty-four thousand collections of <s>dharma</s> (<s>dharmaskandha</s>) have been proclaimed. // Sda_16 //
all other practices serve that purpose, [proceeding] through correct conventional [truth] (<s>tathyasaṃvṛti</s>). // Sda_17 //

body.translated_text: All is included within <s>dharmatā</s>; liberation, however, comes from the realization of <s>śūnyatā</s>;

children.translated_text: When one practices <s>śūnyatā</s>, [if one neglects] conventional causes such as merit (<s>puṇya</s>),
one is cheated of the next world, not knowing the profound meaning. // Sda_18 //
A person of little learning who relies [on emptiness alone and says] there is no merit,

children.text: naṣṭaḥ kāpuruṣastu saḥ vināśayati durdṛṣṭā // Sda_19 //
children.translated_text: that wretched one is destroyed; wrongly understood,
<s>śūnyatā</s> ruins the dull-witted. Thus spoke master <s>Candra</s> (<s>Candrakīrti</s>): // Sda_19-20 //
Conventional truth (<s>vyavahārasatya</s>) is the means (<s>upāya</s>); ultimate truth (<s>paramārthasatya</s>) is the goal (<s>upeya</s>).

children.text: dvayorvibhedaṃ na hi veda yo sa vrajedapāyaṃ viparītabodhāt /
children.translated_text: One who does not know the distinction between the two goes astray through wrong understanding.
Without relying on convention (<s>vyavahāra</s>), the ultimate (<s>paramārtha</s>) cannot be taught. // Sda_21 //
Without the stairway of correct conventional truth (<s>tathyasaṃvṛti</s>),
it is not possible for the wise to ascend to the pinnacle of the palace of reality (<s>tattva</s>). // Sda_22 //
Just as this appearance of the conventional cannot be obtained in the slightest through reasoning,
ultimate [truth] is [precisely] that unobtainability—[that is] the nature of things (<s>dharmatā</s>) as primordially established. // Sda_23 //
Because it is produced from causes and conditions, the conventional is regarded as having the nature of appearance;
if it is improper to examine [it]—then by whom were the reflected moon and other [illusory things] fabricated? // Sda_24 //
Because [things] arise from various conditions, all appearances are thereby established;

children.text: pratyayānāṃ tu vicchedātsaṃvṛttyāpi na sambhavaḥ // Sda_25 //
children.translated_text: but through the cessation of conditions, even in the conventional, [they] are not possible. // Sda_25 //
Thus, when non-delusion of view arises and the purification of conduct [is achieved],
having avoided the wrong path, one attains the <s>Akaniṣṭha</s> (highest) abode. // Sda_26 //

children.text: āyuṣyamalpaṃ bāhulāśca vidyā āyuḥpramāṇaṃ ca kiyanna vidmaḥ /
children.translated_text: Life is short and the branches of knowledge are many; we do not know the measure of our lifespan;
one should pursue precisely what one desires, just as swans [extract] milk from the midst of water. // Sda_27 //

children.text: arvāgdṛśā mohavaśena cāpi kṣamo na satyadvayanirṇaye 'pi /
children.translated_text: One of limited vision, under the power of delusion, is unable even to determine the two truths;

children.text: uktīrgurūṇāmiha sampratītya nyastaṃ dvayaṃ nāgamataṃ hi satyam // Sda_28 //
children.translated_text: having trusted here the words of the teachers, I have set forth the two truths according to the <s>Nāgārjuna</s> tradition. // Sda_28 //

children.text: rājño 'nurodhena suvarṇadvīpe kṛte 'tra śrāddho yadi vā jano 'dya /
children.translated_text: At the request of the king, this was composed in <s>Suvarṇadvīpa</s> (Golden Island). If people today have faith,

children.text: gṛhṇātu samyak suparīkṣaṇena na śraddhayā naiva ca gauraveṇa // Sda_29 //
children.translated_text: let them accept it properly through careful examination — not through faith alone, nor through mere reverence. // Sda 29 //
Sent by the golden king through the fruit of the teacher, the monk <s>Devamati</s>,

children.text: tasyāgrahāt satyadvayāvatāro yuktyā sudhībhistviha vīkṣaṇīyaḥ // Sda_30 //
children.translated_text: through his insistence, this <s>Satyadvayāvatāra</s> (Entry into the Two Truths) should be examined here by the wise with reasoning. // Sda 30 //

body.translated_text: The <s>Satyadvayāvatāra</s> composed by <s>Ācārya Dīpaṅkara Śrījñāna</s> is concluded.

body.text: tenaiva paṇḍitena anuvādakena vīryasiṃhena cānūdya saṃśodhya ca nirṇītaḥ /
body.translated_text: By that very <s>paṇḍita</s> as translator, and by <s>Vīryasiṃha</s>, it was translated, corrected, and finalized.
